<thought>Based on the ¹H NMR data, the molecule shows a methyl singlet (3 H) at 2.23 ppm, two equivalent methylene triplets (2 H each) at 2.81 and 2.98 ppm (J ≈ 7 Hz), and nine aromatic protons (7 H at 7.17 ppm, 2 H at 7.90 ppm). This pattern matches a phenyl‑ethyl‑acetyl (phenethyl acetate) structure: an acetyl methyl attached to a carbonyl, a –CH₂‑CH₂‑ linker attached to a phenyl ring, and the phenyl ring is unsubstituted (5 H) while the carbonyl‑attached phenyl is monosubstituted (4 H), giving a total of nine aromatic protons. The SMILES for phenethyl acetate is **CC(=O)OCCc1ccccc1**. This SMILES reproduces the observed proton pattern and integrates correctly.</thought>
<final_answer>CC(=O)OCCc1ccccc1</final_answer>
